The Pomona Superior Court serves the residents of Pomona and the surrounding communities in Los Angeles County, California. As one of the 58 superior or trial courts in the state, it handles a wide range of civil, criminal, family law, probate, juvenile, and other cases each year. Read on to learn more about the court's history, organization, operations, and services.

Overview of Pomona Superior Court

History

The Pomona Superior Court has a long history dating back to the late 1800s. Pomona itself was founded in 1875, and the need for a local courthouse and justice system grew as the city's population expanded. The original Pomona Courthouse opened in 1898. Over the decades, the court's jurisdiction and caseload continued growing. The current main courthouse opened in 1998 to meet the need for additional courtrooms, offices and services.

Jurisdiction

As a superior trial court in California, the Pomona Superior Court has jurisdiction over all civil, criminal, family law, probate, juvenile and other cases arising within its boundaries. Its service area covers the cities of Pomona, Claremont and La Verne. The court handles an average of over 50,000 new cases filed each year.

Location and Courthouses

The main Pomona Superior Court building is located at 400 Civic Center Plaza in downtown Pomona. This 10-story courthouse contains over 30 courtrooms along with court administration offices. The court also utilizes specialized courtrooms at other county facilities. Criminal and traffic cases are heard at the Pomona Courthouse South facility. Certain family law matters are heard at the Governor George Deukmejian Courthouse in Long Beach.

superior court of pomona Court Organization and Administration

The Pomona Superior Court utilizes the following judicial officers, administrators and staff to serve the public.

Judges and Commissioners

The court currently has 12 judges and 2 commissioners who preside over trials, hearings and other legal matters. The judges are elected officials serving six-year terms. Court commissioners are appointed by the judges to handle certain types of cases and proceedings.

Court Executive Officer

The court executive officer oversees all non-judicial operations, including managing personnel, budgets and facilities. This administrator implements policies set by the court and ensures smooth court functioning.

Court Divisions and Departments

The court is organized into different divisions and departments based on case type. The main ones are Civil, Criminal, Traffic, Family Law, Probate and Juvenile. Within each division, cases may be assigned to specialized departments as needed.v

What Types of Cases are Heard in Pomona Superior Court?

Pomona Superior Court hears a wide variety of cases, including:

Civil Cases

  • Breach of contract
  • Personal injury
  • Property disputes
  • Small claims

The civil division handles all matters involving disputes between two or more parties seeking compensation or other remedies allowed by law. Common civil suits include tort claims, contractual disputes, personal injury cases, medical malpractice, product liability, and real estate cases.

Criminal Cases

  • Traffic violations
  • Misdemeanors
  • Felonies

Criminal cases involve prosecuting those accused of committing misdemeanor or felony crimes. Matters include arraignments, pretrial hearings, motions, trials, sentencing and more. The court oversees misdemeanors, felonies, and traffic infractions committed within its jurisdiction.

Family Law Cases

  • Divorce
  • Child custody
  • Child support

The family law division handles cases involving divorce, child custody and support, spousal support, domestic violence restraining orders, paternity, and adoptions. Many parties represent themselves in these emotional and complex proceedings.

Probate Cases

Probate matters involve distributing the assets of persons who have died or managing the affairs of living persons unable to care for themselves. Proceedings cover wills, trusts, conservatorships, guardianships, and estate disputes.

Juvenile Cases

Juvenile court handles cases involving minors, such as juvenile delinquency, truancy, guardianships, and other matters. The goal is serving the best interests of the child while protecting the public.

How to File a Case in Pomona Superior Court

If you need to file a case in Pomona Superior Court, you can do so by visiting the courthouse in person or filing online. Here's how:

Filing in Person

  • Visit the Pomona Superior Court in person.
  • Fill out the appropriate forms.
  • Pay the filing fee.

Filing Online

  • Visit the Los Angeles County Superior Court website.
  • Register for an account.
  • Fill out the appropriate forms.
  • Pay the filing fee.

What to Expect in Pomona Superior Court

Appearing in court can be a daunting experience, but knowing what to expect can help ease your nerves. Here's what you can expect when appearing in Pomona Superior Court:

Check-In

Upon arrival at the courthouse, you'll need to check in with the court clerk. They will verify your information and provide you with instructions on where to go next.

Security Screening

All visitors to the courthouse must go through a security screening process. This involves passing through a metal detector and having your bags and belongings scanned.

Courtroom Appearance

When your case is called, you'll need to enter the courtroom and take a seat. The judge will preside over the case, and the attorneys will present their arguments and evidence.

Verdict

Once all the evidence has been presented, the judge will make a ruling on the case. This ruling will be final and binding.

How to Find Pomona Superior Court

Pomona Superior Court location

Pomona Superior Court is located at 400 Civic Center Plaza, Pomona, CA 91766. The courthouse is easily accessible by car or public transportation.

Pomona Superior Court Location

The Pomona Courthouse is located at 400 Civic Center Plaza, Pomona, CA 91766. It is easily accessible by public transportation, and there are several parking options nearby. Upon arriving at the courthouse, you will need to check-in with the court clerk and go through a security screening process.

Pomona Superior Court Case Search

If you need to search for a case in the Pomona Superior Court, you can do so online through the Los Angeles County Superior Court website. The website provides a case search tool that allows you to search by case number, party name, or filing date. You can also access court calendars, case summaries, and register for eFiling and eService.

Pomona Superior Court Department

Pomona Superior Court Department O is a division of the court that handles criminal cases. It is located on the second floor of the courthouse and has several courtrooms. If you have a criminal case pending in Pomona, you will likely appear before a judge in Department O. Make sure to arrive early and dress appropriately for your court appearance.

Pomona Courthouse Phone Number

If you need to contact the Pomona Courthouse, you can call their main phone number at (909) 620-3030. However, keep in mind that court staff cannot provide legal advice or represent you in court. If you need legal assistance, it's best to consult with an attorney.

Pomona Superior Court Judges

The Pomona Superior Court has several judges who preside over cases in various departments. Each judge has their own unique style and approach to the law, so it's essential to do your research and prepare accordingly. You can find information about Pomona Superior Court judges on the court's website or through legal directories.

Court Services and Programs

The Pomona Superior Court provides helpful services and programs including:

Self-Help Services

The court's self-help center provides information and assistance to unrepresented parties on how to file court papers and navigate various case matters and procedures. Workshops, information packets and access to attorney assistance are resources offered.

Alternative Dispute Resolution

To help parties resolve disputes without trial, the court offers mediation services in child custody, civil harassment, limited civil cases, probate, small claims, and unlawful detainers. Settlement conferences are also scheduled to settle civil lawsuits.

Jury Service

Jurors play a vital role in the justice system. When called, citizens must report for jury selection and service on criminal or civil trials as required. The court makes reasonable accommodations for those facing hardships.

Interpreters

To ensure due process for all, professional interpreters are provided at no cost for parties who do not fluently speak or understand English. Interpreters for American Sign Language are also available.

pomona court Accessing Court Records and Calendars

The Pomona Superior Court provides both online and in-person access to public case records and court calendars:

Online Access

Many court records can be accessed through the court's Online Case Access system. Users can search case details, obtain document images, check upcoming hearings and trial dates, and more. Remote audio access to live courtroom proceedings is also available in many cases.

Viewing Records at the Courthouse

Case files and records can also be reviewed in person at the courthouse by request. Different departments have varying procedures, so contact the specific clerk's office for instructions. Court calendars listing scheduled proceedings are posted at the courthouse and available from clerks.

Conclusion

Facing legal trouble can be stressful, but knowing what to expect when appearing in Pomona Superior Court can help ease your worries. Whether you're filing a case or appearing in court, this guide has provided you with all the information you need to navigate the process with confidence.

FAQs

  1. What types of cases does Pomona Superior Court hear?

Pomona Superior Court hears civil, criminal, and family law cases.

  1. How do I file a case in Pomona Superior Court?

You must complete the proper petition or complaint forms and submit them to the court clerk along with any required filing fees or fee waiver application. Forms and instructions are available at the clerk's office or court self-help center.

  1. What should I expect when appearing in Pomona Superior Court?

You should expect to check-in with the court clerk, go through a security screening process, and appear before the judge in a courtroom.

  1. Where is Pomona Superior Court located?

Pomona Superior Court is located at 400 Civic Center Plaza, Pomona, CA 91766.

  1. Can I file a case online with Pomona Superior Court?

Yes, you can file a case online through the Los Angeles County Superior Court website.

What are the Pomona Superior Court's hours?

The main courthouse is open Monday through Thursday from 7:30 am to 4:30 pm, and Fridays from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm, excluding court holidays. Different departments may have varying hours. Check the court's website or call for details.

Where can I find Pomona Superior Court local rules?

The court's Local Rules outline policies, requirements and procedures for practicing before this court. They are published on the court's website in the Local Rules tab.

How can I have my traffic ticket case heard at the Pomona Courthouse?

To transfer your traffic case to Pomona, you must file a Transfer to Pomona Courthouse form available on the court website or at the clerk's office. Follow all instructions and submit by the deadline given.

How can I serve on a Pomona Superior Court jury?

You can complete the online jury questionnaire on the court website. If qualified, you will be randomly selected from voter rolls and DMV records and summoned by mail. You may request an excuse from service if you have a valid hardship.
